Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Alicia Torres (Nimbus CTO), Samir Patel (Nimbus Eng Mgr), Lena Cho (Nimbus SRE), Diego Ramirez (Nimbus PM)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on follow-up from reliability incident on 2026-03-09 (timeouts, 5xxs, rate-limit cascades). Reviewed initial RCA hypotheses, observed request patterns, client retry behavior, and mitigation approaches (server-side throttle, retry/backoff, dedicated capacity). Agreed on targeted tests and artifacts to exchange.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run about 45 minutes; main goal is to follow up on the 5xx/timeouts you hit on Monday and agree the testing plan. Jonas will walk through the traces we pulled.
[00:18] Jonas (Redwood): Hi all, I pulled the request traces and a few stack dumps. First caveat — some of the hostnames in the logs got munged by our anonymizer so you'll see slightly off service names.
[00:27] Alicia (Nimbus): that's fine. the important thing is to see request IDs and timing. we saw spikes around 02:12 UTC and again at 02:40 where latency shot up and some requests returned 5 00s.
[00:40] Samir (Nimbus): to be clear, these are users hitting our prompt-based triage flow. throughput isn't huge — maybe 30 qps burst — but we have some long prompts.
[00:52] Jonas (Redwood): yeah we're seeing long seq lengths on those requests (1.2k tokens typical) so KV cache pressure increases. couple notes: 1) some 5xx are upstream timeouts from the model worker; 2) other 5xx correlate with transient gRPC errors between router and worker; 3) rate-limiter kicked in for some token-throttled routes.
[01:12] Lena (Nimbus): do you have a breakdown of which routes hit the rate-limiter? we suspect our billing-tier routing might be misconfigured.
[01:20] Jonas (Redwood): preliminary — majority were the /generate-chat route and a batch of embedding calls we backfilled. we'll share a CSV of route counts in the artifacts.
[01:33] Priya (Redwood CSM): quick note — yesterday's quickfix increased client-side retries from 1 to 3 which reduced visible errors but introduced duplicated load. could be part of the cascade.
[01:46] Diego (Nimbus): oh that explains why we saw a second spike. the client retry backoff was short, like 200ms, so retries became concurrent with original traffic.
[01:55] Maya (Redwood): exactly — retries without jitter and backoff can double/triple traffic and push you into bursty rate limit territory.
[02:04] Alicia (Nimbus): what do you recommend changing first? server-side throttle, longer retries, or move to dedicated capacity?
[02:12] Jonas (Redwood): short term: tune client retries (exponential backoff + jitter, cap retries), and use idempotency keys for non-idempotent requests where possible. Also add a client-side concurrency limit. Medium term: consider dedicated capacity to avoid noisy-neighbor rate limiting.
[02:28] Samir (Nimbus): are there config knobs on Redwood side to lower the impact quickly? can we enable per-customer warm pools or prefix KV caching?
[02:36] Jonas (Redwood): we can enable more aggressive KV prefix caching for your common prompt templates which cuts cold-start token cost and avoids KV thrash. Warm pools are available on Dedicated; for Hosted we can provision burst capacity - but that has cost implications.
[02:51] Lena (Nimbus): we need to understand the tradeoff with latency; caching might help but if it increases tail latency during cache misses that's bad.
[03:00] Jonas (Redwood): fair point. caching helps average cost and throughput but you still need enough worker concurrency to handle cache misses. we recommend a hybrid: prefix cache + autoscaling targets tuned for your p95 SLO.
[03:12] Priya (Redwood CSM): I'll capture the follow-ups and pricing for burst/dedicated options.
[03:18] Maya (Redwood): Jonas, can you walk through a specific trace?
[03:23] Jonas (Redwood): sure — pulling trace id 9f8c... at 02:12:14 UTC. Timeline: client sends request, router forwards to worker, worker begins tokenization, hits kv cache miss, replays large kv fetch, worker blocks on disk read for ~350ms, upstream gRPC retry expires and router returns 502. Then client retried after 200ms, which requeued another request — same path repeats.
[03:46] Alicia (Nimbus): that 350ms disk read is concerning. is that model checkpoint I/O or a swap from GPU RAM?
[03:53] Jonas (Redwood): looks like a model sharding hot swap — when a worker had to pull a shard from S3-backed tier because of memory pressure. our runtime evicts less-used shard segments which can cause cold fetches. Normally we prefetch for common prefixes but this prompt pattern was slightly different.
[04:10] Samir (Nimbus): are there telemetry knobs to alert when shard fetch latency exceeds X ms so we can preemptively scale?
[04:18] Jonas (Redwood): yes — we can add SLO alerting on shard fetch p95 and also surface it in the console. We'll add an alert rule for p95 > 200ms for shard fetches.
[04:27] Diego (Nimbus): on rate limits, do you have per-route vs global limits? our observed 429s were per-customer token throttles i think.
[04:35] Maya (Redwood): Redwood has layered rate limits: per-route, per-customer token bucket, and global ingress. In this case the customer token bucket hit a short window due to retries and batching.
[04:46] Lena (Nimbus): what about backoff recommendations? we need specifics for our client lib.
[04:50] Jonas (Redwood): recommended: exponential backoff starting at 300ms, multiplier 2, jitter 0.25, max retries 3 for idempotent calls, for non-idempotent calls use idempotency keys + max retries 1. Also cap outstanding requests per client to 8. We'll paste a snippet in the slack doc.
[05:05] Alicia (Nimbus): good — we'll make that change and run the load test locally.
[05:10] Priya (Redwood CSM): one more note — we observed a small number of 5xx that had signatures of GC pauses on the worker host — we should surface host-level metrics (CPU, mem, GPU util) around incidents.
[05:22] Jonas (Redwood): absolutely. I'll attach host metrics and GPU utilization for the incident window. There's one host that had elevated swap activity.
[05:30] Samir (Nimbus): about dedicated capacity — what's the SLA tradeoff? does Dedicated avoid these shard fetches entirely?
[05:36] Jonas (Redwood): Dedicated gives you reserved pools so you don't get preempted, and you can pin model variants to those hosts to reduce shard churn. It reduces cold-fetch frequency but doesn't eliminate it if your working set exceeds the pool. We can size a pool based on your p95 seq length and concurrency.
[05:54] Maya (Redwood): cost-wise we'll include a sizing estimate in the pricing doc. For immediate relief we can also enable a short warm pool window for hosted to keep hot shards resident for longer.
[06:06] Diego (Nimbus): what's the expected timeline to get the logs you mentioned?
[06:10] Jonas (Redwood): I can extract the relevant traces, anonymize them, and upload by end of day tomorrow — 2026-03-12. They will include request IDs, route, token counts, and worker host IDs.
[06:19] Alicia (Nimbus): will you include the client request payload or truncated prompts? we need enough to see template similarity for caching decisions.
[06:26] Jonas (Redwood): we'll include truncated templates — not full PII. we scrub anything that looks like PHI per our data handling agreement.
[06:34] Lena (Nimbus): PHI scrubbing is essential — thanks.
[06:37] Priya (Redwood CSM): on the action items, who owns the retry test run?
[06:41] Lena (Nimbus): I'll run the retry/backoff matrix in staging and share results by Friday. We'll test 1,2,3 retries, jitter vs no-jitter, and different concurrency caps.
[06:51] Samir (Nimbus): we'll also try a client code change to ensure idempotency keys for the triage update calls.
[06:57] Maya (Redwood): great. Any blockers for us providing dedicated capacity trial?
[07:01] Alicia (Nimbus): main blocker is cost approval and SOC2 docs for procurement. If you share SOC2 and network topology we've been asked, procurement can fast-track.
[07:11] Priya (Redwood CSM): we'll send SOC2 and network diagrams by 2026-03-14. I'll drop them in your shared folder.
[07:18] Diego (Nimbus): one more technical question — when you say 'token-throttled routes' are those enforced at the router or worker? we need clarification for implementing client throttles.
[07:26] Jonas (Redwood): token bucket enforcement is at the router layer, pre-routing, so requeued retries still hit token accounting. If you implement client-side concurrency and backoff, you'll reduce pressure before it reaches the router.
[07:38] Alicia (Nimbus): ok makes sense. We'll pair the client change with your log artifacts and re-run the test.
[07:45] Maya (Redwood): recap: Redwood shares traces + host metrics (Jonas) by 2026-03-12, Redwood shares SOC2 & network docs (Priya) by 2026-03-14, Nimbus runs retry/backoff matrix (Lena) by 2026-03-13, Redwood to provide dedicated sizing and pricing (Maya) by 2026-03-15.
[08:05] Samir (Nimbus): can we get a short runbook for mitigation steps if we hit similar spikes in prod?
[08:11] Jonas (Redwood): yes — we'll provide a 1-page ops runbook: emergency flags, immediate config flips (client concurrency, temporary burst enabling), and who to page. We'll put that in the shared doc.
[08:22] Alicia (Nimbus): thanks, that will be very helpful.
[08:25] Maya (Redwood): any final questions?
[08:28] Diego (Nimbus): none from me.
[08:30] Lena (Nimbus): all good.
[08:32] Priya (Redwood CSM): I'll create the shared folder and post links after the call.
[08:36] Maya (Redwood): great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up on the artifacts and reconvene next weekly sync.
[08:42] Alicia (Nimbus): thanks, bye.

Notes: transcript contains a few transcription artifacts; speaker labels consolidated where automated transcripts were unclear. References to internal job/host ids redacted for privacy.
